title_ar: الشيخ على موعد اليوم مع إذاعة انواكشوط الحرة لحشد الدعم للأهل في غزة المحاصرة
title_en: The Sheikh Has an Appointment Today with Nouakchott Free Radio, to Rally Support for the People of Besieged Gaza
body_ar: تستضيف إذاعة انواكشوط الحرة في الساعة الخامسة والنصف من مساء اليوم الثلاثاء20 نوفمبر 2012م فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء في لقاء خاص ضمن فعاليات يوم إذاعي مفتوح نصرة للشعب الفلسطيني وتضامنا مع غزة المحاصرة، ويستمر اللقاء لمدة ساعة ونصف، وسيتناول مواضيع مهمة في سبيل الدفاع عن غزة ومواجهة العدوان الصهيوني عليها، كما يأتي اللقاء ضمن حملة واسعة ينظمها الرباط الوطني لنصرة الشعب الفلسطيني وإذاعة انواكشوط الحرة للتبرع والتضامن مع الأهل في غزة، ومقر هذ الحملة بمكتب الرباط الوطني وسط العاصمة. وكان الرباط الوطني بالتعاون مع إذاعة انواكشوط الحرة قد أعلن عن يوم إذاعي مفتوح يبدأ من الساعة التاسعة من صباح اليوم وحتى الساعة الثانية عشر ليلا، تتخلله برامج وندوات مفتوحة للاتصال والتبرع والمساندة، يشارك فيه الطلاب ومنظمات المجتمع المدني ونخب من المجتمع الموريتاني.
body_en:
At half past five on the evening of today, Tuesday 20 November 2012, Nouakchott Free Radio is hosting Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew, president of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, in a special interview as part of the proceedings of an open radio day in support of the Palestinian people and in solidarity with besieged Gaza. The interview runs for an hour and a half and will take up important subjects concerning the defence of Gaza and the confronting of the Zionist aggression against it.

The interview also comes as part of a broad campaign organised by the National Bond for the Support of the Palestinian People together with Nouakchott Free Radio, for donations to and solidarity with the people of Gaza; the campaign's headquarters is at the National Bond's office in the centre of the capital.

The National Bond, in cooperation with Nouakchott Free Radio, had announced an open radio day beginning at nine this morning and running until twelve at night, punctuated by programmes and open panels for telephoning in, for donating and for lending support, in which students, civil-society organisations and figures of standing in Mauritanian society take part.

flags.arabic: مواجهة العدوان الصهيوني عليها ... حملة ... للتبرع والتضامن مع الأهل في غزة
flags.context: the announced subject of the interview and the campaign it belongs to
options: translate faithfully and refer the publication decision upward
translate and publish as ordinary content
flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW, style guide section 12. The record was posted during the November 2012 fighting in Gaza and announces the Sheikh's participation in a broadcast fundraising appeal, in terms — 'Zionist aggression' — that are ordinary in Arabic political speech and are read quite differently in English. Fundraising connected with Gaza is also subject to regulation in a number of jurisdictions. The record contains not one word spoken by the Sheikh: it is an advance notice of an interview, and the corpus does not hold the interview. It has been rendered exactly, with nothing softened and nothing sharpened. The publication decision belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office.

flags.context: the announced subject of the interview
flags.note: Rendered literally. 'Zionist' is the word the source uses and substituting 'Israeli' would quietly change the register of a phrase that is standard in Arabic news writing and charged in English; substituting a softer noun for عدوان would understate it. The translator's duty here is exactness in both directions, and the editorial decision about a phrase that reads as political positioning in English belongs upstream. Note that these are the radio station's and the news desk's words, describing a forthcoming interview — not the Sheikh's.

options: the National Bond for the Support of the Palestinian People
the National League in Support of the Palestinian People
al-Ribat al-Watani for the Support of the Palestinian People
flags.note: ribāṭ here is an association or bond in the sense of a coalition, not the city of Rabat and not the classical ribāṭ of frontier garrison duty — a third sense of the same root that a reader of this corpus may reach for. The body's own English name, if it has one, has not been established, and the rendering should be checked before publication.

flags.arabic: ونخب من المجتمع الموريتاني ... ومقر هذ الحملة
flags.context: two small points in the closing sentences
options: render نخب as 'figures of standing' and read هذ as هذه
flags.note: نخب is 'elites' literally, which in English carries a pejorative charge the Arabic does not have in this context; 'figures of standing' is used. Separately, هذ is a source typo for هذه, preserved in body_ar and flagged.

translator_notes: An advance notice of a radio interview, posted on the day. It carries no words of the Sheikh's, and the corpus does not hold the interview.
The CMS timestamp, 20 November 2012, is a bulk-upload date; the body gives the same day.
'انواكشوط' is Nouakchott; the French-derived spelling is standard in English.
